mainTopic: How much must one eat to be liable for אבר מן החי (a limb from a living creature)? The גמרא challenges the view (stated before this section, attributed to רב) that a כזית is needed, using two ברייתות that seem to say even a tiny amount is enough.
overview: The amud opens by answering a challenge from רב's own statement, which says that a live kosher bird makes one liable for any amount. The גמרא explains that the meat may be tiny, but together with the sinews and bones it adds up to a כזית. Next comes a ברייתא where רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון argue about someone who ate a whole live bird smaller than a כזית. רב נחמן gives the same answer: a little meat plus sinews and bones. The גמרא then asks whether such a bird exists, and the answer is a kosher bird built like the bony קלניתא. רבא then shows how 'thought about food' could change the result for each תנא, and he defends this against אביי: each person is judged by his own thought. Finally, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue over which פסוק forbids אבר מן החי, בשר מן החי and בשר מן הטרפה. The גמרא shows how their views change the number of sets of lashes. It then begins to raise a contradiction, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A teaching that a live bird is forbidden in any amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a statement of רב. It says that one who eats a kosher bird while it is alive is liable for any amount, but if the bird is dead he is liable only for a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone ate a kosher bird alive, he is liable for any amount. If it was dead, he is liable only for an olive-sized amount. If it was a non-kosher bird, he is liable for any amount, whether he ate it alive or dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a statement of רב to challenge the opinion that אבר מן החי needs a כזית. רב says a live bird makes one liable for 'any amount.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view under attack says one is liable for אבר מן החי only for a כזית. רב's statement says that eating a live kosher bird makes one liable בכל שהוא, even for less than a כזית. That looks like a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher species of bird
Any amount at all, even less than a כזית
An olive-sized amount, the usual minimum for punishment for eating
A non-kosher species

phrases.english: If one ate a kosher bird while it was alive –
he is liable for any amount,
if it was dead – only for an olive-bulk,
and a non-kosher bird, whether alive or dead –
he is liable for any amount,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָכַל צִפּוֹר טְהוֹרָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ – בְּכׇל שֶׁהוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge that began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that one is liable for אבר מן החי only for a כזית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's statement makes one liable for eating a live bird בכל שהוא, which suggests no כזית is needed.

steps.title: A little meat plus sinews and bones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'any amount' means a small amount of meat. Together with the sinews and bones, it adds up to a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it means a small amount of meat together with sinews and bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the view that a כזית is needed. It reads רב's statement as talking about a tiny bit of meat that reaches a כזית once the sinews and bones are counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Any amount' refers only to the meat, which can be tiny. The whole limb, including sinews and bones, still totals a כזית. So רב's statement does not contradict the view after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, using the same answer given before
A tiny amount
Sinews and bones

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the answer means 'no כזית needed.' It means the meat alone can be tiny, as long as the meat, sinews and bones together reach a כזית.

phrases.english: Here too
it means a small amount of meat with sinews and bones.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי בְּמַשֶּׁהוּ בָּשָׂר גִּידִים וַעֲצָמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב's statement in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Any amount' means less than a כזית in total.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Any amount' refers to the meat alone. With sinews and bones the total is a כזית.

steps.title: רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון argue about a whole small bird
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: someone ate a whole live bird smaller than a כזית. רבי exempts him, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון makes him liable using a קל וחומר. If the bird was strangled first, everyone agrees a כזית is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone took a bird that was smaller than an olive-bulk and ate it, רבי exempts him and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון makes him liable. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון said: it is a קל וחומר. If one is liable for a single limb of it, surely he is liable for the whole bird! If he strangled it and then ate it, everyone agrees he is liable only for an olive-bulk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא to challenge the view that a כזית is needed. In this ברייתא, one תנא makes a person liable for eating a whole bird that is smaller than a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reasons that eating a single limb makes one liable, so eating the whole live bird should too. His argument assumes that a limb makes one liable even without a כזית. Once the bird is strangled, it is dead, and everyone requires a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts from punishment
Holds liable
An argument from a lesser case to a greater one
A limb
He strangled it, so it died without proper slaughter

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: נָטַל צִפּוֹר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כְּזַיִת וַאֲכָלוֹ –
phrases.english: if one took a bird that did not have an olive-bulk and ate it –
phrases.notes: The bird here is alive and kosher. That is why the case is about אבר מן החי.

phrases.english: Rabbi exempts him,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְחַיֵּיב.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Shimon holds him liable.
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon said:
It is an a fortiori inference,
for a limb of it he is liable,
for all of it, is it not all the more so!
If he strangled it and ate it –
all agree he is liable only for an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נָטַל צִפּוֹר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כְּזַיִת וַאֲכָלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, the גמרא brings a second source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that one is liable for אבר מן החי only for a כזית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's קל וחומר assumes that a single limb makes one liable even with less than a כזית.

steps.title: Even רבי seems to need no כזית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows what the two תנאים really argue about: whether a live creature counts as already divided into limbs. It points out that both of them seem to agree a limb needs no כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagree about this: one Sage holds that even while alive, a creature stands to be divided into limbs. The other Sage holds that while alive, it does not stand to be divided into limbs. But at least everyone agrees that we do not need an olive-bulk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא analyzes the argument in the ברייתא to sharpen the challenge. It shows that the challenge works against both opinions, not just one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי exempts only because he thinks a whole live creature is not seen as made of separate limbs. He does not exempt because a כזית is missing. So both תנאים agree that a separate limb makes one liable without a כזית, and that makes the challenge stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: They only disagree about this point
It stands to be divided into limbs, so its limbs count as separate
According to everyone
At least, in any case

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between רבי and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון is about whether a live creature counts as divided into limbs. It is not about the size needed.

phrases.english: They only disagree here,
because one Sage holds:
phrases.notes: This first Sage is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and the second one is רבי.

phrases.english: while alive, it stands to be divided into limbs,
and one Sage holds:
while alive, it does not stand to be divided into limbs.
But at least according to everyone,
we do not require an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי, אֶלָּא דְּמָר סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא from step 3 to make the challenge sharper.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that one is liable for אבר מן החי only for a כזית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both תנאים assume a separate limb makes one liable without a כזית. Their only argument is whether a whole live bird counts as a collection of limbs.

steps.title: רב נחמן: a little meat plus sinews and bones
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the ברייתא is talking about a small amount of meat together with sinews and bones, which add up to a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: it means a small amount of meat, together with sinews and bones.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the second challenge with the same idea the גמרא used earlier. The whole limb, sinews and bones included, reaches a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Smaller than a כזית' in the ברייתא refers to the meat alone. With the sinews and bones added, the total reaches a כזית. So the view that a כזית is needed still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat

steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges are answered the same way. For אבר מן החי, the sinews and bones count together with the meat toward the כזית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that a limb is measured as a whole, sinews and bones included, when checking whether it reaches a כזית.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
It means a small amount of meat,
together with sinews and bones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: בְּמַשֶּׁהוּ בָּשָׂר, גִּידִים וַעֲצָמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the sharpened challenge from steps 3–4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bird was smaller than a כזית in total, so no כזית is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the meat was smaller than a כזית. With sinews and bones the total is a כזית.

steps.title: Can one limb have a כזית when the whole bird does not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב נחמן's answer: is there a bird whose whole body has less than a כזית of meat, but one limb reaches a כזית with meat, sinews and bones?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there any bird that does not have a כזית of meat in its whole body, yet one limb has a כזית when you add a little meat to the sinews and bones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן's answer from Step 5. It asks whether such a bird even exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 3 the ברייתא was about a whole bird smaller than a כזית. רב נחמן said one limb reaches a כזית once you add the sinews and bones. The גמרא finds it strange that a single limb could reach a כזית when the whole bird is so small.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there really such a thing? A way of saying a case sounds impossible
A tiny amount
Sinews
Bones
A limb

phrases.english: But is there anything,
that in its whole body does not have an olive-bulk of meat,
yet in one limb there is an olive-bulk
made of a small amount of meat together with sinews and bones?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's answer in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's explanation that a small amount of meat with sinews and bones adds up to a כזית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case seems physically impossible: the whole bird is smaller than a כזית of meat, yet one limb supposedly reaches a כזית.

steps.title: Yes, a very small, scrawny bird
steps.stepSummary: רב שרביא answers that such a bird exists: the קלניתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שרביא said: Yes, a קלניתא is like that.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שרביא answers the challenge by naming a real bird that fits the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קלניתא has very little meat but a lot of bone and sinew. So its whole body has less than a כזית of meat, but one limb with its bones can still reach a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: A small, scrawny bird with little meat
Yes

phrases.english: Rav Sherevya said:
Yes, with a kelanita.
phrases.notes: A קלניתא is a tiny, bony bird with very little meat on it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a real case that fits
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No bird could fit רב נחמן's case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קלניתא fits: little meat, but enough bone and sinew in one limb.

steps.title: But a קלניתא is not a kosher bird
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the end of the ברייתא needs a כזית for a strangled bird, but a קלניתא is non-kosher, and רב says a whole non-kosher bird is forbidden in any amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the last part of the ברייתא: if he strangled it and ate it, everyone agrees he needs a כזית. But a קלניתא is a non-kosher bird, and רב said that for a non-kosher bird, alive or dead, any amount makes one liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב שרביא's answer using the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that for a strangled bird everyone needs a כזית. If the bird were a קלניתא, which is not kosher, רב's rule says eating the whole bird makes one liable for any amount, even when dead. So the ברייתא cannot be talking about a קלניתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a teaching
He strangled it (it died without proper שחיטה)
Everyone agrees
A non-kosher bird

phrases.english: Say the last part:
If he strangled it and ate it,
everyone agrees he is liable only for an olive-bulk,
but a kelanita is a non-kosher bird,
and Rav said:
A non-kosher bird, whether eaten while alive
or after it died, makes one liable for any amount!
phrases.notes: רב means when someone eats the whole non-kosher bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב שרביא's answer in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שרביא's claim that the ברייתא is about a קלניתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's last part needs a כזית for a dead bird, which cannot fit a non-kosher bird, since רב says any amount is enough for that.

steps.title: A kosher bird similar to a קלניתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the ברייתא means a kosher bird that is small and scrawny like a קלניתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means a bird like a קלניתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adjusts רב שרביא's answer so it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case does not need an actual קלניתא. It only needs a kosher bird built the same way: little meat and a lot of bone. That fits the whole ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, like

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's tiny bird is a kosher bird built like a קלניתא, with very little meat but enough bone and sinew in one limb to reach a כזית.

phrases.english: Rather, a bird similar to a kelanita.
phrases.notes: He means a kosher bird that is small and bony like a קלניתא.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about an actual קלניתא, a non-kosher bird.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a kosher bird shaped like a קלניתא.

steps.title: Planning to eat it limb by limb makes him liable
steps.stepSummary: רבא says: if רבי holds that a person's thought about food matters, then someone who planned to eat the bird limb by limb but ate it whole is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If you say that רבי holds that thought about food counts, then if someone planned to eat the bird limb by limb and then ate all of it at once, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא goes back to רבי's opinion from Step 3 and adds a new idea: a person's plan can change the bird's status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי exempted someone who ate a whole tiny bird, because a whole creature is not a 'limb'. רבא says that if a person's plan for food matters, then planning to eat it limb by limb gives the bird the status of separate limbs. So even though he ate it whole, he is liable for a limb from a living creature.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say; offering a possibility, not stating it for sure
A person's thought or plan about food
Limb by limb
Liable to punishment

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying for sure that רבי holds this. He says 'if you say' — only if רבי holds that thought matters does this result follow.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If you will say that Rebbi holds
that thought about food counts as thought,
then if he planned to eat it limb by limb,
and ate all of it, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about רבי's opinion from Step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If רבי holds that thought about food matters, a person who planned to eat the bird limb by limb is liable even if he ate it whole.

steps.title: How can the same act make one person liable and not another?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: is there anything where another person who ate it would not be liable, but this person is liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is there really something where if someone else ate it he would not be liable, but if this person eats it he is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's idea from Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבא, two people could eat the very same whole bird. The one who planned to eat it limb by limb is liable, and the other is not. אביי finds it strange that the same food and the same act could lead to different results.

keyTerms.meaning: Another person
He is not liable

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But is there anything,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִילּוּ אָכֵיל לֵיהּ אַחֵר – לָא מִיחַיַּיב,
phrases.english: that if another person ate it, he would not be liable,
but if this one eats it, he is liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וּמִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's idea that a person's plan decides whether the bird counts as limbs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same food and the same act should have the same law for everyone, so one person's thought should not change it.

steps.title: Each person is judged by his own thought
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: yes, each person is judged by his own thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This one is judged by his thought, and that one is judged by his thought.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his idea and accepts that different people can get different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not back down. Since thought about food matters, the result depends on each person's plan. The one who planned to eat it limb by limb is liable, and the one who did not plan that is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his own thought or plan

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, if thought about food matters, the same act can make one person liable and another not, depending on what each one planned.

phrases.english: He said to him:
This one is judged by his thought,
and that one is judged by his thought.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the outcome and explaining why it makes sense
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The same act must have the same law for every person.
steps.terutzMaskana: When thought matters, each person's liability follows his own plan.

steps.title: רבא's mirror case: planned to eat it dead, but ate it alive
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that if רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון holds that thought about food counts, then someone who planned to eat the bird dead but ate it alive is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: If you say that רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון holds that a thought about food counts as a real thought, then if someone planned to eat the bird after it died, but he ate it alive, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second case that is the opposite of his first one. Here the person's thought makes him exempt rather than liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, the person's thought made him liable. Here the person thought of the bird as food to be eaten after it died. He did not think of it as something to be split into limbs while it was alive. So by his own thought, eating it alive does not count as eating a limb from a living creature, and he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: A person's thought or intention about how something will be eaten as food
If you say, meaning if we assume this is the view
Dead and alive
Exempt, meaning he gets no punishment

phrases.english: And Rava said:
If you say

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: that Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Shimon holds
that thought about food is considered thought,
if he intended to eat it dead,
and he ate it alive – he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the mirror case of רבא's statement in step 10, where thought led to liability. Here thought leads to exemption.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון, someone who planned to eat the bird dead but ate it alive is exempt, because his thought decides the matter.

steps.title: אביי asks again: can one person be exempt for what makes another liable?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks how one person can be exempt for eating something that would make another person liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is there really anything where, if someone else ate it, he would be liable, but if this person ate it, he is exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's new case. He asks the same kind of question he asked in step 11, but now in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same live bird would make an ordinary eater liable. אביי finds it strange that one person's private plan could take away a punishment from the same act. Normally the law about a food seems to depend on the food itself, not on the eater.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anything at all? This is a sharp question that suggests no such thing exists
He is liable to punishment

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But is there anything
that if another person ate it, he would be liable,
but if this person ate it, he is exempt?

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the person who planned to eat the bird dead is exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same act of eating would make someone else liable, so it seems wrong that this person's thought could make him exempt.

steps.title: רבא answers: each person is judged by his own thought
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that each person is judged according to his own thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This person is judged according to his thought, and that person is judged according to his thought.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי with the same principle he used in step 12. Each eater's liability depends on his own plan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees that two people can get different results for the same act. Once thought about food counts, the thought belongs to each person. So one person's plan can make him liable while another person's plan makes him exempt, in either direction.

keyTerms.meaning: This one goes according to his own thought

steps.whatToRemember: As רבא explains, if thought about food counts, a person's thought can make him liable (רבי's view, step 10) or exempt (רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון's view, step 13). Each person is judged by his own thought.

phrases.english: He said to him:
This one is according to his thought,
and that one is according to his thought.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה לְפִי מַחְשַׁבְתּוֹ, וְזֶה לְפִי מַחְשַׁבְתּוֹ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the claim in the question and explains why it is not a problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Liability depends only on the food itself, so the same food must give the same result for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Liability follows each eater's own thought, so different eaters can get different results.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's sources for a limb and flesh from a living animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says one פסוק is the source for אבר מן החי, and a second פסוק is the source for בשר מן החי and בשר מן הטרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: "You shall not eat the life with the flesh" is the source for a limb from a living animal. "And you shall not eat any flesh that is torn in the field" is the source for flesh from a living animal and flesh from a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: which פסוקים are the sources for these prohibitions. רבי יוחנן gives his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, "the life with the flesh" covers only a whole limb from a living animal. Plain flesh cut from a living animal, which is not a full limb, comes from the פסוק about a טרפה. He puts it together with flesh from a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb cut from a living animal
Flesh (not a complete limb) cut from a living animal
An animal with a deadly injury or defect, which is forbidden to eat
The life, here meaning the animal while it is still alive

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up אבר מן החי (a whole limb, with flesh, sinews, and bones) with בשר מן החי (just a piece of flesh). The whole argument in this step and the next is about which פסוק covers the plain piece of flesh.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
"You shall not eat the life with the flesh" –
this is a limb from a living animal,
"And you shall not eat any flesh that is torn in the field" –
this is flesh from a living animal
and flesh from a tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא תֹאכַל הַנֶּפֶשׁ עִם הַבָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the פסוק sources, after the thought discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "The life with the flesh" forbids אבר מן החי. "Flesh torn in the field" forbids בשר מן החי and בשר מן הטרפה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש puts flesh from a living animal under the first verse
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says "the life with the flesh" covers both a limb and flesh from a living animal, while "flesh torn in the field" covers only flesh from a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: "You shall not eat the life with the flesh" is the source for a limb from a living animal and flesh from a living animal. "And you shall not eat any flesh that is torn in the field" is the source for flesh from a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש disagrees with רבי יוחנן about which פסוק covers plain flesh from a living animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only difference between them is בשר מן החי. רבי יוחנן puts it under the טרפה פסוק, while ריש לקיש puts it under "the life with the flesh" together with a whole limb. For ריש לקיש, the טרפה פסוק is left only for flesh from a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Flesh taken from a טרפה animal

steps.whyThisMatters: Which פסוק a prohibition comes from decides how many sets of lashes someone gets when he eats two kinds together. The next step spells this out.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
"You shall not eat the life with the flesh" –

phrases.aramaic: זֶה אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי וּבָשָׂר מִן הַחַי,
phrases.english: this is a limb from a living animal and flesh from a living animal,
"And you shall not eat any flesh that is torn in the field" –
this is flesh from a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different view from רבי יוחנן's in step 16. They disagree only about the source for בשר מן החי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "The life with the flesh" forbids both אבר מן החי and בשר מן החי. "Flesh torn in the field" forbids only בשר מן הטרפה.

steps.title: How many sets of lashes: three combinations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the practical difference between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. Two forbidden items from the same פסוק give one set of lashes, and items from two different פסוקים give two.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone ate a limb from a living animal and also flesh from a living animal, רבי יוחנן says he gets two sets of lashes and ריש לקיש says only one. If he ate flesh from a living animal and also flesh from a טרפה, ריש לקיש says two and רבי יוחנן says only one. If he ate a limb from a living animal and also flesh from a טרפה, everyone agrees he gets two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is showing what the argument from the last two steps changes in real life. It does this by counting how many sets of lashes a person gets in three different eating cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is simple: if both items come from the same פסוק you get one set of lashes, and if they come from different פסוקים you get two. רבי יוחנן puts בשר מן החי together with טרפה, while ריש לקיש puts בשר מן החי together with אבר מן החי, so their counts flip. A limb plus טרפה flesh always comes from two different פסוקים, so both sages say two.

keyTerms.meaning: A whole limb cut off from a living animal
A piece of flesh (not a whole limb) cut off from a living animal
Flesh from a טרפה, a fatally injured or sick animal
Liable twice, meaning two separate sets of lashes
According to everyone; both sides agree

steps.whatToRemember: Same פסוק means one set of lashes, two different פסוקים means two. רבי יוחנן groups בשר מן החי with טרפה. ריש לקיש groups בשר מן החי with אבר מן החי. A limb plus טרפה flesh gives two according to both.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up who says what. Each sage says 'one' exactly in the pair that he puts under one פסוק, so the answers swap between the first two cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a disagreement about how to read the פסוקים into a real difference in punishment. It also sets up the 'everyone agrees' case that the גמרא is about to challenge.

phrases.english: If one ate a limb from a living animal
and flesh from a living animal,
according to Rabbi Yochanan he is liable twice,
according to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish
he is liable only once.
If one ate flesh from a living animal
and flesh from a tereifa,

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ חַיָּיב שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish he is liable twice,

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת.
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yochanan he is liable only once.
If one ate a limb from a living animal
and flesh from a tereifa,
according to everyone he is liable twice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָכַל אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי וּבָשָׂר מִן הַחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the practical results of the disagreement between רבי יוחנן (step 16) and ריש לקיש (step 17).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Limb plus בשר מן החי: רבי יוחנן says two sets of lashes, ריש לקיש says one. בשר מן החי plus טרפה: ריש לקיש says two, רבי יוחנן says one. Limb plus טרפה: everyone says two.

steps.title: Setting up a contradiction to the 'everyone agrees' case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that it is about to bring a source that seems to contradict what was just said.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing to quote a source that seems to clash with the claim that everyone agrees a limb plus טרפה flesh gives two sets of lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וּרְמִינְהוּ means 'and they threw them against each other,' which signals that two sources seem to contradict. The source itself is quoted at the start of the next amud.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a challenge to the last case of step 18, where everyone agreed he is liable twice.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that everyone agrees one who eats a limb from a living animal and flesh from a טרפה gets two sets of lashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A contradicting source is about to be quoted. This line only signals that the challenge is starting.
